authority: gate/up/down on a real layer only. Damage is applied to an in-memory copy; no artifact is written.

bench.machine: Apple host CPU; receipt/header metadata only
bench.rule: no hardware measurement claim without hardware

claim_boundary: Static sidecar artifact. No hardware measurement.

kinds.low_rank: best rank-10% approximation of the slice - is the information redundant rather than absent
kinds.noise: Gaussian at the slice's own scale, so magnitude is not confounded with importance
kinds.quantize: 2-bit uniform within the slice's own range - can it be CHEAPER, which is the question a smaller representation actually asks
kinds.zero: delete the slice - can this information be REMOVED

matched_by_construction: fraction selects the same share of rows or columns in every kind, so two kinds at one fraction touch the same element count. Across DIFFERENT-SIZED tensors it does not, which is why elements_destroyed is reported on every point.
not_capability: hidden-state cosine two layers downstream is not capability. FIDELITY_HIERARCHY forbids refusing a capability claim at this bar, and CAPABILITY_STAGES is where the deeper rungs live.
output_is: one curve point: fraction, elements_destroyed and the hidden-state cosine two layers downstream, at the named kind
why_three_were_missing: only zero existed, and zero can only answer whether information can be DELETED. A route to 2.0 BPW needs to know whether it can be CHEAPER, and those are different questions.
